q: What is the PRIMARY function of a SIEM platform?
opts: Encrypt data at rest on endpoints
Replace the need for endpoint protection
exp: SIEM centralizes, normalizes, and correlates telemetry to produce actionable alerts and provide an investigative record. It does not encrypt data, replace endpoint controls, or deploy patches.
tip: SIEM value depends on log source coverage, parsing quality, synchronized time, and tuned correlation rules.

q: A detection rule fires 200 times per day, and analysts confirm all instances are legitimate administrative activity. What is the BEST action?
opts: Delete the rule to remove the noise
Leave it and tell analysts to ignore
Route alerts to an unwatched mailbox
exp: Tuning preserves detection capability while removing known-benign patterns, and testing confirms the rule still catches real activity. Deleting the rule creates a blind spot, and instructing analysts to ignore alerts or hiding them guarantees a missed detection.
tip: Tune with narrow, documented exclusions (specific accounts, hosts, and processes), never by disabling the whole detection.

q: Why should logs be forwarded to a central platform rather than retained only on the originating host?
opts: Central storage uses less total disk space than local storage
Local logs cannot record security events
Central logging removes the need for time synchronization
exp: Centralization protects log integrity against anti-forensic deletion and enables cross-source correlation. Central storage generally uses more space, hosts can log locally, and accurate time synchronization becomes even more important when correlating sources.
tip: Send logs off-host in near real time to append-only or write-once storage — this is a favorite exam and audit control.

q: Which data source shows which hosts communicated, on which ports, and how much data moved, without capturing packet payloads?
exp: Flow data summarizes conversations and volumes, making it efficient for long retention and exfiltration detection while omitting content. Full packet capture includes payloads at high storage cost, Windows security logs record host-level events, and SNMP polling retrieves device status.
tip: Flow data is ideal for spotting beaconing and large outbound transfers; packet capture is needed when you must see content.

q: Which mechanism allows a network device to notify a monitoring system immediately when a threshold or failure condition occurs?
opts: SNMP traps sent from the device to the manager
Scheduled SNMP polling by the manager only
Manual review of device console output
exp: Traps are unsolicited notifications pushed by the device when an event occurs, providing lower latency than polling intervals. Polling detects conditions only at each interval, and manual review or configuration backups are not alerting mechanisms.
tip: Use SNMPv3 for authentication and encryption; v1 and v2c send community strings in cleartext.

q: Which standard allows automated tools to exchange configuration checklists and vulnerability data in a common format for compliance scanning?
exp: SCAP standardizes formats and identifiers (including CVE, CPE, CCE, and CVSS) so tools can consistently assess configuration and vulnerability state. The other protocols handle email, remote administration, and voice signaling.
tip: SCAP-validated tools evaluate benchmarks such as CIS or DISA STIGs automatically and produce comparable results.

q: An EDR platform detects credential-dumping behavior on a workstation. Which immediate automated response BEST limits damage while preserving investigation options?
opts: Isolate but keep it powered on
Shut the host down and unplug it
Delete the suspicious process binary and take no further action
exp: Network quarantine halts lateral movement and command and control while retaining volatile evidence and continued telemetry. Reimaging destroys evidence, shutdown loses memory artifacts, and deleting a binary leaves the intrusion unexamined.
tip: Automated containment is high value, but define exclusions so critical servers are not isolated without human review.

q: A regulation requires that security logs remain available for three years, but the SIEM retains only 90 days of searchable data. What should be implemented?
opts: Delete at 90 days and note the gap
Keep archives on the SIEM indexers
exp: Tiered retention with immutable archive storage satisfies long-term requirements economically while keeping recent data searchable. Reducing verbosity loses evidence, deletion violates the requirement, and consolidating everything on primary indexers is costly and does not address immutability.
tip: Know the difference: retention (how long you keep it), archiving (where it lives long-term), and preservation (legal hold overrides both).

q: Which web filtering approach protects users who are off the corporate network without backhauling traffic to headquarters?
opts: A centralized on-premises proxy requiring VPN for all traffic
exp: Endpoint agents and cloud gateways enforce policy wherever the user connects. On-premises proxies require tunneling all traffic back, perimeter rules only see traffic crossing that perimeter, and manual hosts files are unmanageable and easily bypassed.
tip: Web filter features to know: URL scanning, content categorization, reputation scoring, and block rules.

q: Which control blocks resolution of known malicious domains before a connection is even attempted?
opts: Protective DNS filtering with a threat-intelligence-driven sinkhole
An outbound firewall rule permitting all port 443 traffic
exp: DNS filtering prevents resolution of malicious names, stopping many attacks early and cheaply, and the sinkhole reveals which hosts attempted the lookup. Proxies and antivirus act later in the chain, and permissive firewall rules provide no protection.
tip: Enforce internal DNS use and block external resolvers and DoH bypass, or clients can evade DNS filtering entirely.

q: Which DNS-based mechanism specifies what receiving servers should do with messages that fail authentication checks and provides reporting to the domain owner?
exp: DMARC publishes policy (none, quarantine, or reject) based on SPF and DKIM alignment and enables aggregate and forensic reporting. SPF authorizes sending hosts, DKIM cryptographically signs messages, and MX records designate mail servers.
tip: SPF = who may send. DKIM = signature proving integrity and origin. DMARC = policy plus alignment plus reporting.

q: An organization publishes SPF and DKIM but still receives spoofed messages that appear to come from its own domain. Which configuration is MOST likely missing?
opts: A DMARC policy set to reject
exp: Without an enforcing DMARC policy, receivers have no instruction to reject unaligned mail even when SPF and DKIM exist. Key length, MX records, and relay counts do not determine handling of spoofed mail.
tip: Roll out DMARC gradually: p=none to gather reports, then quarantine, then reject once legitimate senders are aligned.

q: Which detection approach identifies previously unknown attacks by flagging deviations from established normal behavior?
exp: Anomaly and trend analysis compares observed activity against a baseline, enabling detection of novel attacks at the cost of more false positives. Signatures and hashes detect only known patterns, and port filtering makes no behavioral judgment.
tip: Signature detection: precise, low false positives, blind to new attacks. Anomaly detection: catches novelty, needs a good baseline.

q: Which pairing correctly matches an operating system security mechanism to its platform?
opts: Group Policy for Windows; SELinux for Linux
Group Policy for Linux kernel modules; SELinux for Windows registry settings
Both mechanisms apply only to network appliances
Both mechanisms are legacy antivirus engines
exp: Group Policy centrally enforces Windows configuration in a domain, while SELinux implements mandatory access control policy on Linux by confining processes. The other pairings misattribute platforms and purposes.
tip: SELinux enforces labels regardless of file permissions — a process confined by policy cannot exceed it even as root.

q: A device connects to the corporate LAN with outdated antivirus and missing patches. Which technology can place it in a remediation VLAN until it complies?
exp: NAC evaluates device posture at connection time and can grant, deny, or quarantine access pending remediation. WAFs inspect web requests, DNS sinkholes block malicious resolution, and load balancer health checks assess server availability.
tip: NAC decisions can combine identity (802.1X), device certificate, and posture (patch level, AV status, encryption state).

q: Which capability builds behavioral profiles for each user and alerts when activity deviates significantly, such as a payroll clerk suddenly querying engineering repositories at 2 a.m.?
exp: UEBA baselines normal behavior per identity and entity, then scores deviations to detect insider threats and compromised accounts. Signature scanning finds known malware, port security limits MAC addresses, and pinning validates certificates.
tip: UEBA is the go-to answer for insider threat and compromised-credential detection scenarios.

q: An analyst must allow a partner to reach only an internal SFTP server on port 22 from one source address. Which rule is correct and MOST restrictive?
opts: Permit that source IP to port 22 only
Permit any source to that server
Permit all their traffic and log it
exp: Least privilege in firewall terms means specifying source, destination, protocol, and port as narrowly as possible with an explicit deny after. The alternatives grant unnecessary breadth in source, destination, or port range.
tip: Rule specificity checklist: source, destination, protocol, port, direction, and time restrictions where supported.

q: Which practice MOST reduces the risk of orphaned accounts after employees leave?
opts: A monthly reminder email to managers
exp: Integrating identity lifecycle with the authoritative HR record removes accounts promptly and consistently, and reconciliation catches gaps. Manual reminders, self-service deletion, and annual cleanup all leave active credentials for extended periods.
tip: Joiner-mover-leaver automation is the expected answer for account lifecycle questions.

q: A government system assigns every file a classification label and every user a clearance, and the operating system enforces access strictly by these labels regardless of the file owner's wishes. Which access control model is this?
exp: MAC enforces system-wide labeling and clearance rules that users cannot override. DAC lets owners grant access at their discretion, RBAC assigns rights via job roles, and ABAC evaluates multiple attributes in policy expressions.
tip: MAC = labels and clearances, no owner discretion. It is the model in classified and SELinux-style environments.

q: An access policy grants entry if the user is in the Finance department, on a managed device, connecting during business hours, from an approved country. Which model does this represent?
exp: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes of subject, resource, action, and environment in a policy decision. RBAC would consider role membership alone, DAC relies on owner-granted permissions, and MAC uses labels and clearances.
tip: ABAC is the model behind conditional access and Zero Trust policy engines — expect it in modern scenarios.

q: A hospital grants permissions by job function — nurse, physician, billing clerk — and moving an employee to a new role automatically changes their access. Which model is in use?
exp: RBAC binds permissions to roles rather than individuals, so role changes update access consistently. Rule-based control applies conditional rules such as ACL criteria, DAC is owner-driven, and MAC uses labels and clearances.
tip: RBAC scales well and simplifies audits, but watch for role explosion and users accumulating multiple roles.

q: Which combination represents true multifactor authentication?
opts: A password and a hardware security key
A fingerprint and a retina scan
Two different passwords stored in a password manager
exp: MFA requires factors from different categories: something you know plus something you have. A password and PIN are both knowledge factors, two biometrics are both inherence factors, and multiple passwords remain a single category.
tip: Categories: something you know, something you have, something you are, and somewhere you are (location).

q: Which second factor is MOST resistant to real-time phishing proxy attacks?
opts: A push notification with approve or deny
A TOTP code from an authenticator app
exp: FIDO2 credentials are cryptographically bound to the relying party origin, so a proxy site cannot use them. SMS codes and TOTP values can be relayed by an attacker-in-the-middle site, and push approvals are vulnerable to fatigue attacks.
tip: Phishing-resistant MFA on the exam means FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys, passkeys, or certificate-based authentication.

q: A fingerprint reader is tuned so that fewer unauthorized people are accepted, but authorized users are rejected more often. Which metrics changed?
opts: Both false acceptance and false rejection rates decreased
The crossover error rate is now zero
exp: Tightening a biometric threshold trades convenience for security: FAR falls while FRR rises. Both rates cannot fall simultaneously by threshold adjustment alone, and the crossover error rate is the point where they are equal rather than zero.
tip: CER (crossover error rate) is the standard accuracy comparison: lower CER means a better biometric system.

q: Which protocol uses XML-based assertions to convey authentication and attribute statements between an identity provider and a service provider for web SSO?
exp: SAML exchanges XML assertions for federated web single sign-on. OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework issuing access tokens (with OpenID Connect layering authentication on top), RADIUS provides network AAA, and Kerberos uses tickets within a realm.
tip: SAML = enterprise web SSO with XML. OAuth = delegated authorization. OIDC = authentication built on OAuth with JSON/JWT.

q: An application needs to verify who the user is and receive standardized identity claims from a provider. Which technology is appropriate?
opts: OpenID Connect on top of OAuth
OAuth 2.0 alone, which is designed for authorization
LDAP bind operations over the internet
exp: OIDC adds an authentication layer and ID tokens containing identity claims to OAuth 2.0. OAuth alone delegates authorization without asserting identity, internet-exposed LDAP is inappropriate, and SNMPv3 authenticates device management sessions.
tip: Misusing OAuth access tokens as proof of identity is a classic design flaw — the exam expects OIDC for authentication.

q: A university lets students use their campus credentials to access a third-party library service without creating new accounts. Which concept enables this?
opts: Credential sharing through a common password
Local account replication to the vendor's database
exp: Federation establishes trust so one organization's identity provider authenticates users for another's service without duplicating credentials. Shared passwords and replicated account databases increase risk and administrative burden, and anonymous access provides no identity.
tip: Federation reduces password sprawl but concentrates risk in the identity provider — protect it with strong MFA and monitoring.

q: Quarterly, each manager reviews a report of their team's system entitlements and formally confirms or revokes each one. What is this process called?
exp: Attestation is the periodic certification of access rights by an accountable reviewer, correcting entitlement creep. Identity proofing verifies who a person is during enrollment, provisioning creates accounts, and federation extends trust between organizations.
tip: Attestation catches accumulated permissions from role changes and temporary projects — a standard audit requirement.

q: Before issuing credentials to a new remote employee, the organization validates a government ID and performs a live video verification. Which process is this?
exp: Identity proofing establishes that a person is who they claim to be before credentials are issued. Attestation reviews existing access, authorization determines permissions, and accounting records activity.
tip: Weak enrollment undermines every downstream control — including the help desk reset process, a common attack target.

q: An organization wants administrators to hold no standing privileged rights, instead requesting elevation that is granted for 60 minutes with full session recording. Which capability is this?
exp: Just-in-time access grants time-bound privileges on request, eliminating standing rights that attackers target. Password vaulting stores and rotates credentials but may still allow persistent access, DAC is an access model, and SSO addresses authentication convenience.
tip: PAM components: vaulting, credential rotation, session recording, JIT elevation, and ephemeral credentials.

q: Which password policy BEST reflects current guidance?
opts: Written passwords stored at the desk
exp: Modern guidance (NIST SP 800-63B) emphasizes length, breached-password screening, and MFA over forced rotation and byzantine complexity rules, which drive predictable patterns. Short passwords, aggressive expiration, and physical notes weaken security.
tip: Rotate immediately on suspected compromise. Otherwise, prefer length, breach screening, MFA, and a password manager.

q: Which approach BEST describes passwordless authentication?
opts: A long password in a manager
exp: Passwordless authentication relies on cryptographic credentials held on the device (often unlocked by biometrics), so no reusable secret is transmitted or stored on the server. Managed passwords and emailed codes still involve shared secrets, and anonymous access is not authentication.
tip: Passkeys are phishing-resistant and eliminate credential reuse — the direction modern guidance favors.

q: A manufacturing plant restricts shop-floor accounts to their assigned shifts. Which control is being applied, and what benefit does it provide?
exp: Time-based restrictions limit when authentication is permitted, reducing off-hours misuse and making anomalies more visible. MAC concerns labels, federation extends identity trust, and accounting records rather than restricts activity.
tip: Pair time restrictions with alerting: an attempt outside allowed hours is a high-quality detection signal.

q: A user is a member of two groups: one granting Read on a folder and another denying Write. The user also has an explicit Allow Write permission on the folder. In a typical Windows environment, what is the effective outcome?
opts: The explicit deny on Write takes precedence, so writing is blocked
The explicit allow overrides the group deny, so writing is permitted
Permissions cancel out and access is fully denied
The user receives Full Control by default
exp: Deny permissions generally take precedence over allow permissions in Windows NTFS evaluation, so an applicable deny blocks the action. Permissions do not cancel to a total denial, and Full Control is never granted implicitly.
tip: Rule of thumb: deny overrides allow; effective permissions are cumulative otherwise, and share plus NTFS yields the most restrictive result.

q: A DLP deployment blocks so many legitimate business emails that staff begin using personal accounts. What is the BEST corrective approach?
opts: Disable DLP entirely to restore productivity
Block all outbound email attachments permanently
Ignore the personal email usage since DLP is working as designed
exp: Overly broad DLP drives users to unmonitored channels, which is worse than the original risk; tuning with classification and sanctioned exception paths restores balance. Disabling DLP removes protection, blanket blocking worsens workarounds, and ignoring shadow channels leaves data uncontrolled.
tip: Roll out DLP in monitor mode first to measure false positives, then enforce progressively on the highest-confidence rules.

q: Which statement BEST distinguishes XDR from EDR?
opts: XDR runs only on network appliances and ignores endpoints
EDR provides broader coverage than XDR
XDR is a legacy antivirus technology
exp: XDR extends detection and response by correlating signals from multiple domains, providing broader attack-chain visibility than endpoint-only EDR. The other statements invert or misstate the relationship.
tip: MDR is different again: a managed service where a provider operates detection and response on your behalf.

q: Which trade-off correctly describes agent-based versus agentless monitoring?
opts: Agents are deeper; agentless is easier
Agents fail when a host is off-network
exp: Agents see local detail continuously and report from anywhere, at the cost of management overhead; agentless approaches avoid installation but need network access and credentials at scan time. Agents actually work better off-network, and network monitoring remains necessary for unmanaged devices.
tip: Most mature programs use both: agents on managed endpoints and agentless discovery to find what has no agent.

q: An application must transfer files to a partner with confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication. Which protocol and port combination is appropriate?
exp: SFTP runs within an SSH session on port 22, providing encryption, integrity, and host authentication. FTP and TFTP are cleartext protocols without integrity protection, and HTTP is unencrypted.
tip: SFTP (SSH-based, port 22) differs from FTPS (FTP over TLS, ports 989/990). Both are secure; know which one the question describes.

q: After an alert is triaged and remediated, which step ensures the response actually worked?
opts: Validation that the host is clean
Closing the ticket immediately after remediation is attempted
Deleting the alert from the SIEM
Reporting the incident count in the monthly metrics only
exp: Validation confirms remediation effectiveness before closure, catching persistence mechanisms and reinfection. Immediate closure, deleting alerts, and metric reporting do not verify the outcome.
tip: Alert handling cycle: detect → triage → investigate → contain/remediate → validate → tune → document.

q: Which practice BEST secures service accounts used by automated processes?
opts: Domain admin rights to avoid errors
One shared account for all apps
exp: Non-interactive restriction, least privilege, managed rotation, and monitoring contain service account risk, which is a common lateral movement path. Excessive rights, account sharing, and spreadsheet-documented static passwords are all high-risk antipatterns.
tip: Prefer managed identities or group managed service accounts where the platform handles rotation automatically.

q: Which firewall design element places internet-facing services in a network segment that can be reached from the internet but has tightly restricted access into the internal network?
exp: A screened subnet (DMZ) is bounded by filtering so external clients reach published services while inbound access to internal networks stays restricted. A flat network provides no separation, an air gap allows no connectivity at all, and guest wireless serves untrusted clients rather than published services.
tip: Screened subnet rules should permit only the specific ports the published service needs, in both directions.

q: An antivirus console shows 40 endpoints with definitions more than 30 days old. What is the MOST significant risk?
opts: The console will run out of storage
Those endpoints will lose network connectivity
Definition age has no security relevance
exp: Stale definitions leave known threats undetected on those hosts, and the reporting gap may also indicate agents that have stopped communicating entirely. Console storage and connectivity are unrelated, and definition currency clearly matters for signature-based detection.
tip: Track agent health as a metric: installed, running, current, and reporting. Any of those failing means unmonitored assets.

q: A developer needs to read production logs to troubleshoot but currently holds full production database write access. Which change applies least privilege MOST precisely?
opts: Read-only access to the logs needed
Unchanged access plus a ticket each use
exp: Least privilege scopes access to the specific resource and action needed, with time limits and auditing. Ticket requirements without access reduction leave excessive rights, complete removal impedes legitimate work, and environment-wide read access is broader than necessary.
tip: Least privilege has three dimensions: which resources, which actions, and for how long.

q: Which scenario BEST justifies deploying file integrity monitoring?
opts: Improving web server response time under load
exp: FIM detects unauthorized changes to critical files and is explicitly required by standards such as PCI DSS. Performance, encryption, and load distribution are handled by other technologies.
tip: FIM answers the integrity half of CIA and is one of the few controls that catches web defacement and backdoored binaries quickly.

q: Which protocol is a directory access protocol commonly used to query user and group information, and which port secures it?
opts: LDAP, secured as LDAPS on TCP 636
Kerberos, secured on TCP 88 with TLS
RADIUS, secured on UDP 1812 with TLS
exp: LDAP queries directory objects and is protected as LDAPS on TCP 636 (or via StartTLS on 389). SAML is an assertion protocol rather than a directory service, Kerberos uses port 88 without requiring TLS for its ticket exchange, and RADIUS on 1812 traditionally uses its own shared-secret protection.
tip: Ports worth memorizing for this domain: 389 LDAP, 636 LDAPS, 88 Kerberos, 1812/1813 RADIUS, 49 TACACS+.

q: Which monitoring activity would FIRST reveal that a new server was deployed without the approved security baseline?
opts: Checking the office badge access logs
exp: Compliance scanning compares actual configuration to the required baseline and flags deviations quickly. Training records, badge logs, and financial reports contain no configuration state.
tip: Pair compliance scanning with deployment automation so new systems start compliant rather than being corrected later.

q: A newly deployed inline IPS blocks a critical business application because a signature matches its unusual traffic pattern. What is the BEST response?
opts: Switch the IPS to detection-only mode for all traffic permanently
Remove the IPS from the network path
Instruct users to retry until the traffic passes
exp: Targeted exceptions preserve protection elsewhere while restoring the business function, and vendor feedback improves the signature. Globally disabling prevention or removing the device sacrifices protection broadly, and retrying does not address a deterministic block.
tip: Inline prevention requires a tuning period. Start in detection mode, baseline the false positives, then enable blocking progressively.

q: Which authentication token type generates codes on a dedicated physical device that has no network connectivity?
opts: A hard token such as a key fob OTP generator
A soft token app on a smartphone
An SMS message containing a code
An email link for magic-link sign-in
exp: Hard tokens are dedicated hardware devices generating codes offline, which resists malware on general-purpose devices. Soft tokens run on phones, and SMS and email deliver codes over interceptable channels.
tip: Security keys (FIDO2) are a hardware token variant that also resists phishing because they verify the site origin.

q: Which reporting practice MOST improves security operations effectiveness?
opts: Weekly raw log excerpts to executives
Only the blocked spam message count
exp: Operationally meaningful metrics reviewed regularly drive improvement in coverage and response speed. Raw logs are unusable for decision-making, company-wide alert broadcasts create noise and disclosure risk, and single vanity metrics do not reflect capability.
tip: Useful SOC metrics: MTTD, MTTR, true-positive rate, coverage by log source and MITRE technique, and backlog age.

q: Which THREE controls together provide the strongest protection for administrative access to critical infrastructure?
opts: Phishing-resistant MFA on all administrative authentication
Just-in-time elevation with session recording through a privileged access gateway
Separate administrative accounts distinct from daily-use accounts
Shared administrator credentials stored in a team wiki for availability
exp: Strong authentication, time-bound audited elevation, and separation of administrative from routine accounts each close a distinct attack path. Shared documented credentials eliminate attribution and are a severe weakness.
tip: Privileged access answers cluster on: separate admin accounts, MFA, jump/bastion access, JIT elevation, and session recording.
